title: Waymo boosts first debt deal to $5 billion in robotaxi push
source_used: Bloomberg (text read on Transport Topics, which carries the Bloomberg report; the Bloomberg page returned a bot check)
key_facts: Waymo, Alphabet's driverless taxi unit, increased the size of its first debt raise to $5 billion.
Waymo had earlier sought to borrow more than $3 billion for the same first debt deal.
Pacific Investment Management Co. (Pimco), Blackstone and Sixth Street Partners were among the investors.
The deal priced at 5.25 percentage points over the benchmark rate, according to people familiar with the matter.
The loan is allocated and expected to formally close soon; Goldman Sachs arranged it.
Waymo raised $16 billion at a $126 billion valuation earlier this year and has set a goal of 1 million paid weekly rides this year.
Pimco, Blackstone and Goldman Sachs declined to comment; Waymo and Sixth Street did not respond.
quote_evidence: Waymo increased the size of its inaugural debt raise to $5 billion, tapping lenders to help fuel the robotaxi company’s growth as it expands globally.
The loan has been allocated and is expected to formally close soon, the people said.
why_it_matters_hint: Waymo is borrowing more to fund its fleet growth and new cities, which shows how much money robotaxi services need.
